title: Tsitsipas on Medvedev and Zverev: 'I'm a little far from them'

 After beating Aleksandar Kovacevic, Stefanos Tsitsipas opened up about the choices that have shaped his career. Without naming his father, he stressed the importance of having the right team and candidly acknowledged the distance between him and Medvedev and Zverev.
 SHANGHAI, CHINA - OCTOBER 14: Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece returns a ball during the fourth round men's singles match against Daniil Medvedev on day eight of the Rolex Shanghai Masters 2026 at Qi Zhong Tennis Centre on October 14, 2026 in Shanghai, China. © LINTAO ZHANG / Getty Images via AFP Arthur Millot 21/10/2026, 07:36 3 min to read Follow us Tsitsipás Stefanos Tsitsipas is gradually finding his form again on tour.
 After a difficult period, the Greek decided to change his entourage by removing his father, Apostolos, from his team. 
 Remove ads After his victory over Aleksandar Kovacevic (7-6(9), 3-6, 6-3) at the ATP 250 in Almaty, he discussed the importance of having the right people around him, in comments reported by Punto de Break.
 Tsitsipas stresses the importance of his entourage
 “My team represents half of my work.
 It’s an inspiring team that creates a serene atmosphere. It’s very important and pleasant to feel that calm, both in training and in daily life. You have to be surrounded by the right people.
 Throughout my career, I’ve been through a lot of trials. I’ve had to handle some fairly difficult situations. I’m someone who likes to work and who is ready to put in a lot of effort,” he explained in a press conference.
 Without directly naming his father, the former world No. 3 also looked back on the difficulties he faced in the past and on the importance of choosing the right people to work with.
 “Since childhood, I was raised with the belief that everything that matters in life is achieved through work.
 That’s why, when certain things disrupted that vision, I started to feel lost. I had never experienced that before.
 But I think you learn over time and become more careful in your choices, especially regarding the people you want to move forward with in life. Today, I know better who I want to work with.”
 “I write my own story”
 Stefanos Tsitsipas was also asked about the success of players from his generation, such as Daniil Medvedev and Alexander Zverev.
 “I always see things from my own point of view. I follow my own path and I write my own story.
 Their story is not mine, just as mine is not theirs. They wrote their own story through their accomplishments and their successes.
 In a way, I can say that I’m a little far from them today, but it’s my story.
 It’s not just about results and accomplishments, but also everything you have to go through as a player,” he said.
 “I can use all that experience to help the next generation of tennis players”
 Despite the difficulties, the Greek remains hopeful and wants to learn from his experience to get back to his best level.
 “I can use all that experience to help the next generation of tennis players. I see my journey as a permanent learning process.
 It’s a bit like a roller coaster, with a lot of ups, downs and changes along the way. I’ve already had my share of success.
 I’ve won many matches and achieved big victories, and every day gives me the chance to write a new chapter of my own story,” he concluded.
